newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher amid stronger cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher amid stronger cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were expected to open higher Thursday amid early talk of significantly stronger cash, industry sources said.
June over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.20 to $2.22 after settling to the upside Wednesday at $2.184 per mmBtu.

"It's May 1. People got caught short. All of it is adding up to a very nervous market," one trader said, noting cooling demand in the South, heating demand expected in the Northeast and storage injections were boosting cash.
On ACCESS, June last traded 0.2 cent higher at $2.186 after reaching a high of $2.197.
Early cash prices at Henry Hub were talked more than 10 cents higher at $2.22-2.25.
Also helping prop up cash was news that Houston Lighting and Power's 1,250 megawatt South Texas 1 nuclear unit was shut late Wednesday.
Technically, traders said resistance in June was next at $2.24, and then at the $2.385 contract high. Support was seen at $2.05 and then along the up trendline at $2.01.

In Wednesday's cash market, Gulf Coast prices notionally gained more than five cents to about $2.10-15. Midcon pipes were up a few cents to the mid-to-high $1.90s. New York city gate gas also was modestly higher around $2.40.
Cooler weather is expected to blanket most of the Northeast and Midwest by early next week, with some below-normal temperatures already evident in the central U.S.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 25 bcf, at the high side of expectations, and were now 213 bcf, or 33 percent, above year-ago levels. For the same week last year, overall inventories gained 68 bcf.
